title: Replay the historical containment caller with isolated child imports
body:
The registered rational-containment customer authenticates its historical inputs and then launches independent `-I -B` Python children that can still import preexisting bytecode. In a disposable copy, a same-length stale `dot` coefficient (9→8) makes the actual reference adapter reject in `spans()` even after the exact original source bytes and timestamp are restored. Removing only the cache restores the complete original h=10/h=12 payload. This is a reproducibility defect, not acceptance of an invalid mathematical certificate.

This opt-in successor authenticates and retains the original package plus its six historical Git-pinned inputs, then changes only the three `subprocess.run` AST call expressions in `verify.py`, imported `benchmark.py`, and `test_kernel.py`. It preserves every original argument, optimization flag, timeout, arithmetic mutant and scientific assertion. All 13 child/grandchild calls get separate fresh import namespaces. The complete 42,860-comparison transcript, 7,614 targets, full audit payload and original kernel/source/frame/adapter controls remain checked with JSON type preservation. The paired benchmark still runs; its timing ratio is not a correctness requirement or a new performance claim.

Three historical inputs have drifted on current main. This package restores their exact old blobs without revising any source pin; it does not claim the original current-checkout entry passes. The 17 retained files (95,894 bytes) remain byte-identical to their declared origins. All changes are confined to `research/rational-containment-child-isolation/`; frozen inputs, shared runners and the selected frontier are unchanged.

Validation on macOS 27 arm64 / CPython 3.12.2:

- Both registered commands passed, including the full original scientific receipt and 13 actual child/grandchild calls, 14 distinct namespaces, seven successes and six expected rejections; all owned cache directories removed.
- Four optimized test groups passed: nine actual adapter executions across timestamp/unchecked/checked-hash and cache-isolated/cache-removed cases; all 17 retained-source mutations rejected; exact launch grammar and all four original mutants; complete empty-PATH Git-free export with a stale cache, preserving all source and preexisting cache bytes. Registered test phase: 21.787 seconds.
- Metadata/Git pins passed. Committed-byte and source-history preflight passed for all 26 files and both source commits (`410026dc…`, `b58ad9ef…`). Actual committed export and bundle check passed; separate extracted empty-PATH optimized-outer replay matches `RESULT.json`.
- No native Windows/Linux, hosted-CI, repository-wide suite, selected cold replay or hard-kill cache-cleanup claim. This fixed historical caller includes POSIX `resource`; it is not a general Python sandbox or arbitrary-descendant policy.

Canonical claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2988#discussioncomment-19130816

Entry overlap used the complete round-3 cache (506 open PRs, 3,650 Discussion/comment/reply records, 5,860 local notes). Exact-caller searches found no overlapping child-import repair. The frame-closure child-isolation successor, PR2553, PR2990 and isolated-descendant-bytecode retain credit for their earlier boundaries and explicit next-caller handoff. Closed PR bodies, arbitrary diffs and unpublished work were outside that snapshot.

Prepared by JoyboyBrian with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. CubeJerry's containment contribution and all original source credits are retained. No new kappa, supplier admission or full multiplication theorem is claimed.

Scoped submission recheck: the refreshed cache contains 512 open PRs (2026-10-22 19:09 UTC) and 3,673 Discussion records (19:10 UTC), both fully paginated. The exact-caller offline search covered all 5,862 notes at this contribution head (the original 5,860 plus this package's README/TASK), with no missing local paths. Matches were this claim/hub pointer, the original customer, this successor, and existing contextual notes; no competing repair was found. Offline results retain the ordinary limitation that later changes may be absent. Live predecessor reads confirmed PR2553 merged at `a82fea84445e54042fa56b39ff1509fa329fad93` and PR2990 merged at `9158ee6d097e8058b177c54a1f68a6c30249c8f8`.

Submission checkpoint: canonical main was fetched again and remains `b58ad9ef4d4e861b0eaa5dba41742bdc072dca51`, priority revision 7. The refreshed complete inventory (2026-10-22 19:10:08 UTC) covers 512 open PRs, 3,673 Discussion records and 5,860 base local notes. Scoped search and live predecessor heads were rechecked; no competing result was identified in this stated coverage. Closed PR diffs, arbitrary nested code and unpublished work remain outside it.
